raw_response:
I am old now, and I do not like to gamble with the land. These 10.1 mu feed my family, so I will do the same wheat-maize way I know, not try fancy things. For wheat, if I see the soil moisture is okay in early October, I will sow all 10.1 mu then. Wheat cannot be weak going into winter, so I will put base fertilizer first, not too little. Fertilizer is expensive, but if wheat comes up yellow and thin, that is worse. I usually give enough at sowing, then one more topdress around jointing. Water from the well costs money too, so I will not over-irrigate, but wheat here usually needs a few turns of water. I will watch for weeds early and spray once. If rust or aphids show up badly, I will spray, but I do not like spending unless I see a problem.

After wheat harvest in June, I will not delay maize. That gap is very short, so I will clear the straw quickly, do light rotary tillage, and plant maize right away. Maize misses yield if planted late. I will buy hybrid seed like other people nearby use, because saved maize seed is not reliable. I will still put fertilizer, but not in a big wasteful way: some at planting, some later when maize gets taller. If the summer rain is decent, I may only irrigate once, maybe not more. With only two people at home, I depend on machine service at the busy time. I am not chasing the highest yield. I just want a steady crop, not too much cash spent at once, and enough grain income from both seasons.
